title: Evaluating Efficacy and Safety of Berotralstat in Preventing Angioedema Attacks in Subjects With Acquired Angioedema Due to C1 Inhibitor Deficiency (AAE)
official: An Open Label, Single Arm, Explorative Trial to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Berotralstat in Preventing Angioedema Attacks in Subjects With Acquired Angioedema Due to C1 Inhibitor Deficiency (AAE)
summary: The primary aim of the study is to explore the effectiveness of Berotralstat in preventing angioedema attacks in patients with Acquired Angioedema (AAE-C1-INH).
conditions: Acquired Angioedema Due to C1-Inhibitor Deficiency (AAE-C1-INH)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Males and non-pregnant, non-lactating females ≥ 18 years of age
2. Able to provide written, informed consent.
3. Subject weight of ≥ 40 kg
4. A clinical diagnosis of AAE is defined from the following criteria:

   * Recurrent angioedema without wheals
   * No family history of angioedema and/or C1-INH deficiency
   * C1-inhibitor activity level of \<50% of normal and at least 1 of the following:

     * Age at least 40 years at reported onset of first angioedema symptoms
     * Reduced C1q level (below the lower limit of normal), recognizing that normal C1q levels do not exclude the diagnosis of AAE. Absence of a pathogenic variant in the SERPING1 gene encoding for the C1-inhibitor protein.
     * Serologic confirmation of anti-C1-inhibitor antibodies.
5. Access to and ability to use one or more acute medications approved by the relevant competent authority for the treatment of acute attacks of HAE (icatibant, plasmaderived C1-INH).
6. The subject must have at least 2 AAE attacks which meet all the requirements below during the run-in period of 28 days. In case of not recurrence of 2 attacks in 28 days or attacks do not meet all the requirements below, the run-in period will be extended to a maximum of 56 days from the Screening visit:

   * The attacks are unique, which is defined as an attack that does not begin within 48 hours of the end of a previous attack.
   * The attacks must include symptoms of swelling. Symptoms of swelling, in addition to visible swelling, may also include symptoms in the oropharyngeal or abdominal regions which are indicative of internal swelling.
   * The attacks are confirmed by the Investigator to be AAE attacks. Subjects will be contacted within 2 business days of the attack to discuss the attack, any queries on the entered data in the diary, as applicable.
7. In the opinion of the Investigator, the subject is expected to adequately comply with all required study procedures for the duration of the study. The subject must demonstrate adequate compliance with all study procedures required from the screening visit, including diary recording of HAE attacks beginning at the screening visit. Women of childbearing potential and male participants with partners of childbearing potential must agree to use a highly effective method of contraception, throughout the study and for the protocol-defined period after the last dose of the investigational medicinal product (IMP). Acceptable highly effective methods include combined (estrogen- and progestogen-containing) hormonal contraception, progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation, intrauterine devices (IUDs), intrauterine hormone-releasing systems (IUSs), bilateral tubal occlusion, vasectomized partner (provided he is the sole sexual partner), and true sexual abstinence when this is the participant's usual and preferred lifesty.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any clinically significant medical or psychiatric condition or medical history that, in the opinion of the Investigator or Sponsor, would interfere with the subject's ability to participate in the study or increases the risk to the subject by participating in the study
2. Concurrent diagnosis of any other type of recurrent angioedema
3. Any abnormal clinical, laboratory or urinalysis parameter at screening that, in the opinion of the Investigator or any contraindication describe in berotralstat SmPC
4. Known hypersensitivity to the active substance of berotralstat or to any of its excipients
5. Current treatment with any long-term prophylactic therapy intended for the prevention of angioedema attacks, unless the required washout period has been completed before the start of the run-in period. Required washout periods are as follows:

   * plasma-derived or recombinant C1 inhibitor used for long-term prophylaxis: 14 days;
   * lanadelumab: 28 days;
   * berotralstat or any other oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor: 28 days;
   * attenuated androgens (e.g., danazol): 28 days;
   * tranexamic acid: 28 days;
   * any other investigational or approved long-term prophylactic treatment for angioedema: at least 28 days, or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer.

   Use of approved on-demand (rescue) therapies for the treatment of acute angioedema attacks (e.g., icatibant or plasma-derived C1 inhibitor) is permitted throughout the study, including during the run-in period and the treatment period, according to standard clinical practice.
6. Pregnant women
7. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B or C) in alignment with SmPC requirement
